Shook
SHOOK
adjective (Millennial slang)
The past tense of shake used as an adjective for shaken: shocked, rattled, scared, or deeply surprised. The usage is old in AAVE and was spread by hip-hop, notably Mobb Deep’s "Shook Ones" (1995), where it meant scared or weak. In 2016–2017 it went mainstream on Twitter and in memes ("I’m shook") for anything surprising, from a plot twist to a celebrity breakup, and was added to online dictionaries.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

To be shook is to be rattled: stunned by news, scared by something, or simply amazed. "That season finale had me shook." The Christian observation: the slang is harmless, and Scripture has a great deal to say about shaking. People are shaken by fear: when the disciples saw Jesus walking on the sea, "they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear" (Mat 14:26). God Himself shakes things: at Philippi, "there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken" (Act 16:26). And He promises a final shaking of everything that can be shaken, "that those things which cannot be shaken may remain. Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace" (Heb 12:27-28). That is the deepest answer to being shook. The believer’s life can be rattled by bad news, but its foundation cannot be moved: "I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved" (Psa 16:8). Some fear is right; the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and it ought to shake us. But the fear of man and of circumstances is meant to give way to faith. A father tells his children: you will be shook by things in life, by losses, betrayals, and frightening news; when you are, run to the Rock that does not shake, and you will find that the kingdom you belong to cannot be moved.

Webster 1828 Definition

Millennial slang (AAVE; Mobb Deep, 1995; mainstream 2016–2017) for shocked or rattled; harmless, and an opening to Scripture’s kingdom which cannot be moved (Heb 12:28; Psa 16:8).

Key Scripture

Mat 14:26 — "And when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were troubled, saying, It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear."

Act 16:26 — "And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one's bands were loosed."

Heb 12:27-28 — "And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain. Wherefore we receiving a kingdom which cannot be moved, let us have grace, whereby we may serve God acceptably with reverence and godly fear:"

Psa 16:8 — "I have set the LORD always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved."

Psa 62:2 — "He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved."

Modern Corruption

Shook is harmless slang for being rattled; Scripture turns it to the deeper truth that believers belong to a kingdom which cannot be shaken.

expand to see more

There is little to correct in the word. The only drift worth noting is the habit of being perpetually shook: a culture of constant news, outrage, and spectacle keeps young people rattled, startled from one shock to the next, with little sense of anything stable beneath them. Anxiety becomes a lifestyle.

The redemption is a foundation. "He only is my rock and my salvation; he is my defence; I shall not be greatly moved" (Psa 62:2). Teach the young to take shocks seriously without being ruled by them, to bring their fears to God, and to build their lives on what cannot be shaken: the Word, the promises, the kingdom of Christ. Then they can be shook for a moment without being moved.
